stories.title: 借书小任务
paragraphs: Our class has a task at the public library. We must borrow one book, read it and write a short note about it. At the door, we stand in line and wait. A sign asks us not to shout. We obey the rule because other people are reading inside.

I choose a book about birds. My friend wants the same book, so we make a careful plan. I will return it next Tuesday, and then she can borrow it. We write the date on our calendars. A library works well when everyone takes care of its books and thinks about other readers.
translation: 我们班在公共图书馆有一项任务：借一本书，阅读后写简短读书笔记。门口我们排队等候。标志提醒不要大喊。我们遵守规定，因为里面还有其他人在读书。
我选了一本关于鸟的书，朋友也想借，于是我们仔细计划：我下周二归还，她再借。我们把日期写在日历上。人人爱惜书本、为其他读者着想，图书馆才能顺畅运作。

stories.title: 相机的闪光灯
paragraphs: We are inside a museum with our teacher. Each visitor gets a small booklet. A guard shows us a warning: no flash and no touching. I put my camera away, but my friend wants a photo of an ancient cup. She does not know that her flash is on.

Before she can press the button, I point to the sign. We ask the guard what the museum will allow. He explains that we can take a photo without flash. My friend turns it off and thanks him. She also apologises for not checking first. The cup stays safe, and we have a good visit.
translation: 我们跟老师在博物馆参观，每位参观者都拿到一本小册子。门卫给我们看警告：禁止闪光灯和触摸。我收起相机，朋友却想给一个古杯拍照。她不知道闪光灯还开着。
她按按钮前，我指给她看标志。我们问门卫馆内允许怎样拍照。他解释，可以不用闪光灯拍。朋友关掉闪光灯，向他道谢，也为没有先检查而道歉。古杯安然无恙，我们也愉快地完成参观。

stories.titleEn: A Note for a New Friend
paragraphs: A new friend comes to live in our city. Her family is staying on Green Street. I write a note to help her find the library. She should walk along the street, pass the cinema and turn left. The library is between the bank and a little cafe.

Behind the library, there is a garden where we can meet. I add a small map to the note. My friend says that clear directions help her feel less lost. On Saturday, we meet in the garden and read together. Later, she draws a map of her old hometown for me. Now we both know a new place.
translation: 一位新朋友搬到我们城市，她家暂住在格林街。我写便条，帮她找图书馆：沿街走，经过电影院，再向左转。图书馆在银行和小咖啡馆之间。
图书馆后有花园，我们可以在那里见面。我在便条上加了一张小地图。朋友说，清楚的指路让她不那么迷茫。星期六我们在花园见面，一起读书。后来她为我画了老家地图。现在，我们都了解了一个新地方。

stories.title: 感谢社区帮手
paragraphs: Our class wants to thank the people who help our community. A volunteer helps us recycle paper and pick up litter. A gardener shows us how to plant flowers. An engineer explains the new bridge, and an artist helps us draw it. There are many kinds of useful work.

On the way home, we see an officer direct the traffic. Our teacher asks what we can do to help, too. We decide to make thank-you cards and keep our streets clean. Next week, a scientist will visit our school to teach us about water. We have many people to learn from.

stories.title: 有故事的日历
paragraphs: I make a calendar with Grandma. In January and February, we draw winter clothes. In March and April, we add flowers and rain. May has a picture of our family picnic. June has a card for Children's Day. Every page tells us something about our life.

July and August have our holiday plans. September shows the first day of school. October has a red flag. November has brown leaves, and December has a warm bowl of soup. Grandma asks which page I like best. I cannot choose just one. Each month has a different story, and we can add new memories next year.

stories.title: 家乡的节日小册子
paragraphs: Our class makes a festival booklet about our hometown. One page is about Labour Day. We draw people doing useful work. Another page is about the Dragon Boat Festival. My grandparent tells me about a local race and the tradition of sharing rice dumplings. I write down her story.

We also add a National Day page with a family holiday picture. For the class party, we decorate the room with paper lanterns. We celebrate our finished work by reading the booklet together. A festival is more than a date on a calendar. It can help us learn family stories and care about the people around us.
translation: 我们班做一本家乡节日小册子。一页介绍劳动节，画人们做有用的工作；另一页介绍端午节。我的一位祖辈讲述当地比赛和分享粽子的传统，我把故事记下来。
我们还添了国庆节一页，画家庭假日。为了班级聚会，我们用纸灯笼装饰房间。大家一起读完成的小册子来庆祝。节日不只是日历上的日期，还能让我们了解家人的故事，关心身边的人。

stories.title: 在地图上旅行
paragraphs: It is raining, so we travel with a map instead of a suitcase. Dad finds India, and my sister finds Italy. I point to Britain and read about an old castle. Then we find Cairo in Egypt. A picture shows a pyramid and a camel near the desert.

Our next stop is Hawaii. We look at a painting of an island and the ocean. Each place has a different landscape and story. We write the country or place name under each picture. Before lunch, we have made a little world gallery on the table. We can enjoy learning about places even when we stay at home.
translation: 下雨了，我们带着地图而不是行李箱去“旅行”。爸爸找印度，姐姐找意大利。我指着不列颠，读一座古堡的介绍。接着我们找到埃及的开罗，图上有沙漠旁的金字塔和骆驼。
下一站是夏威夷。我们看一幅海岛和海洋的画。每个地方都有不同的风景和故事，我们在图片下写国家或地名。午饭前，桌上就成了小小的世界画廊。待在家里，也能愉快地了解不同地方。

stories.title: 我们共同的家园
paragraphs: Our project compares wild animals from different places. A kangaroo can move across grassland on strong back legs. A koala spends much of its time in trees. We also read about birds that live on a beach and turtles that return to an island. Each animal has a special home.

What do these animals have in common? They all need a healthy environment. Our teacher asks us to think about our own neighbours in nature. We can keep litter out of the river and watch birds quietly. We make a poster to protect these homes. Learning about faraway animals helps us care for the animals nearby, too.
translation: 我们的课题比较不同地方的野生动物。袋鼠能靠强壮的后腿穿过草原，考拉大部分时间待在树上。我们还读了住在海滩的鸟和返回海岛的海龟。每种动物都有特别的家。
它们有什么共同点？都需要健康的环境。老师让我们想想身边的自然邻居。我们可以不让垃圾进入河流，安静地观察鸟儿。我们做海报保护这些家园。了解远方动物，也能帮助我们关心附近的动物。

stories.title: 去博物馆的三种办法
paragraphs: We want to reach the museum early. Dad suggests driving, but there is a lot of traffic. I look at the distance on the map. It is too far to go on foot. My sister suggests a bike ride, but Grandma will come with us. We need a route that works for everyone.

Finally, we choose the underground. Each passenger has a seat on our train, and the station is near the museum. We walk the last short part together. Walking is good for our health, and this little walk is enough for Grandma today. A good travel choice thinks about every person, not just the fastest way.
translation: 我们想早点到博物馆。爸爸建议开车，但路上车多。我查看地图上的距离：全程步行太远。姐姐提议骑自行车，可奶奶也同行。我们需要适合所有人的路线。
最后我们选地铁。车上每位乘客都有座位，车站也离博物馆很近。最后一小段我们一起走。步行有益健康，对奶奶来说今天这样走一小段就够了。好的交通选择要考虑每个人，不只看哪种最快。

stories.title: 旅行计划要问清楚
paragraphs: My cousin wants to visit our hometown. We use the internet with Mum to find information. A map app shows the station and the museum. I want to share local history and culture, so our plan includes a morning museum tour. My cousin also asks about hot pot and seafood.

We look at a menu and choose food together. Mum reminds us to confirm the opening time and the booking. An old blog may have the wrong information. We check the museum's own website before we pack. Now our plan has a clear route, a meal and time to rest. Good planning begins with useful questions.

我们看菜单，一起选餐。妈妈提醒，要确认开放时间和预订；旧博客可能有错误信息。打包前我们查看博物馆自己的网站。现在计划里有清晰的路线、餐食和休息时间。好的计划从有用的问题开始。

stories.title: 一张明信片的旅程
paragraphs: At the end of our tour, I choose a postcard for my friend. It shows the hill we explore with our guide. I want to send a little souvenir, too, but the shop is closed. Maybe a story will be a better gift than another thing.

I write about our train ride, the local food and a kind person who helps us. Dad buys a stamp. I do not need an envelope for the postcard, but I write the address carefully. This small card holds a happy memory and a new experience. Next time, I hope my friend can join us and make a story of her own.

我写火车旅程、当地美食和帮助我们的好心人。爸爸买邮票。明信片不需要信封，但地址要认真写。这张小卡装着快乐回忆和新体验。希望下次朋友能同行，拥有她自己的故事。
